texts: good. both halves parse into one fireable rule: the crowd of nightmoths gathers as a unit at a lantern-row, and each such gathering gets its own descent of sky-cats from the cliff-spires tied back to it. Every compound (nightmoth, lantern-row, sky-cat, cliff-spire) is carried with its kind intact and nothing in the sentence is lost.

good. the "whenever" wording routes straight to a fireable rule, with the settling crowd as the condition and the descent from the cliff-spires as a per-occasion response linked back to that settling; all content is covered.

bad: the response clause "sky-cats stay on the cliff-spires" is a stay-put state rather than a happening, so the translator had to invent an occurrence to hang it on and then filed "on the cliff-spires" with an entity-style link instead of the occurrence's location — the adjudicator ruled the parse defective on exactly that, and the "were already up there and remain" sense ends up with no carrier at all. Rewrite the response as the plain event this rule is really contrasting with: "When a handful of nightmoths gathers at a lantern-row, sky-cats do not descend from the cliff-spires." If the sky-cats' being up on the spires matters in its own right, state it separately the way you already do elsewhere ("Sky-cats roost on the cliff-spires during the day.") rather than packing position and continuation into the response clause.
